oliver (docs): Hey team — opened a PR to merge the retention examples, a short migration plan for audit logs, and a small customer FAQ blurb. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6120 :wave:
sana (security): Thanks. Quick ask: can we use the term 'tokenization' in the external FAQ or stick to 'pseudonymization'? Tokenization is more customer-friendly but we should define it.

ben (legal): I'd prefer 'pseudonymization' in legal copy and a parenthetical note in the FAQ like (also called tokenization) so we don't introduce ambiguity. Also will add a short legal-hold sentence and an exception approval flow.

priya (eng-docs): I'll add py/ts snippets. Plan: show a short KMS-derived-salt example and then recommend calling our vetted crypto helper for production. Also adding a tiny data-classification matrix mapping "low/med/high" to example retention tiers.

oliver (docs): Proposed example TTLs: short=14 days, medium=90 days, long=3 years. Clearly labelled "illustrative only; consult legal/security." Also adding a one-paragraph migration suggestion for teams with raw logs.

sana (security): Please include a note about rotating salts/keys and the re-identification risk of deterministic tokens. Call out that hashing alone isn't sufficient for high-risk PII.

priya (eng-docs): Added a succinct code snippet (illustrative):
```python
# illustrative only - use vetted helper in prod
import hashlib

def pseudo_with_kms_salt(uid, salt):
    return hashlib.sha256((salt + uid).encode()).hexdigest()[:20]
```

priya (eng-docs): And a TS example pointing at the helper: `const token = cryptoHelper.pseudonymize(userId)` (vetted lib).

ci-bot: PR #6120 status: review requested by sana (security), ben (legal).

ben (legal): I'll add two short sentences for top-level policy: "Records are retained only as necessary for business purposes or legal obligations. Retention exceptions require documented approval from Legal and the CISO."

sana (security): Left one small nit on the PR: tighten SOC2 phrasing to "retention determined by business need and legal obligations" and avoid operational steps in the customer-facing blurb. Also request we include a reviewer checklist: TTL sanity, vetted crypto helper usage, linkcheck to infra KMS docs.

oliver (docs): Added the checklist; fixed the FAQ language to be customer-facing and vague on ops. Added a short migration playbook for teams with raw audit logs: 1) snapshot raw logs to restricted archive, 2) run a pseudonymization/redaction backfill into a sanitized dataset, 3) run query parity tests, 4) switch consumers, 5) expire raw archive per approved retention.

priya (eng-docs): I updated the doc to call the infra KMS page at /internal/infra/kms (pinged infra to confirm link). Also added a tiny example approval form for retention exceptions that routes to Legal/CISO.

ben (legal): I'll review wording of exception flow now and add the sample customer-facing FAQ line.

sana (security): Approving the security points; left an inline comment urging we add a short line about auditability of redaction operations for SOC2 evidence.

ci-bot: PR #6120 status: changes requested by sana (security) — address audit trail note.

oliver (docs): Will add a short section on redaction/pseudonymization audit trails (who ran the job, manifest of records affected, checksum). Aiming to get signoff tomorrow and publish a docs note after merge. Thanks all! :rocket:
